jetpack env is the canonical spelling for entering a project environment. jet env becomes a documented thin forward to it, one implementation with two entry points, so the ratified shell auto-activation hook keeps working while the boundary law holds: jet acts on code, jetpack acts on environments. Bare jetpack is reserved for a future interactive TUI and must not enter an environment. jetpack tool run is deleted as the arity-1 case of jetpack use with a trailing command.

Every package reference is written package@source#version. The hash slot answers which version and accepts a literal version or a policy tier such as auto or latest. The prefix spelling, for example the tier written before the name, is deleted; the same meaning is written omp@releases#auto. Plain refs such as ripgrep@nixpkgs are unchanged. The old parse path is removed with no fallback parser retained.

Any verb that reads or executes Jet source belongs to the jet binary. Any verb that acquires, pins, realizes or exposes what your code needs belongs to jetpack. There is no exception. Consequently jetpack dev, jetpack test, jetpack fmt, jetpack build, jetpack run and jetpack enter are deleted, and the hangar verb is removed from the jet binary.

The hangar verb groups everything that manipulates the store rather than the project. It absorbs the former top-level cache, shared-store, vendor, clean and list verbs. The name hangar is kept because it is the existing user-facing name for the object store, so no new word is coined. The doctor verb stays top-level because it is what a stuck user runs first.

A jet verb that needs the project environment while outside it fails with a coded diagnostic and acquires nothing. jetpack env and jetpack use enter silently when the closure is already materialized and confirm once, showing package count and total bytes, when anything must be downloaded. The yes flag skips that prompt. A non-interactive run that would need a download and has no yes flag fails naming the flag, and downloads nothing.

jetpack update determines its scope from the current directory: inside a jetpack project it updates that project. Narrowing flags select dependencies only or tools only, and the default covers everything in scope. It prints one plan naming every moving source with its before and after identity, package count and download size, then applies after a single confirmation. The outdated verb survives separately.

Every tool installed by jetpack is projected as a jetpack shim rather than a hardlink into a read-only store object. The shim execs the real binary for normal use, and when the tool attempts to update itself the shim refuses the in-place write cleanly and offers to move the declarative pin instead. The accepted costs are that jetpack sits in the execution path of every installed tool, and that which reports the shim path.

Realization displays one live aggregate line carrying the current phase with counts, transferred bytes and total bytes, plus one settled row per package as it completes. Byte totals grow honestly as the closure is discovered rather than being fabricated. Output degrades to deterministic plain lines with no terminal, under NO_COLOR, and when piped, and live regions are erased before any diagnostic.
